title: Food supplement safety and market entry in Germany, Bulgaria, North Macedonia and China
journal: Open Access International Journal of Academic Research UNIVERSES
abstract: Objective: To compare market entry controls for food supplements in Germany, Bulgaria, and North Macedonia with the health food framework of mainland China, and assess their relationship to scientific safety evaluation. Methods: A functional comparative legal review of legislation, judgments, and regulatory guidance was combined with a targeted medical literature review. Sources were checked through September 24, 2026. Vitamin B6, green tea extracts, and red yeast rice illustrate dose related toxicity and regulatory responses. Results: Germany uses notification, Bulgaria requires prior registration, and North Macedonia uses a compliance opinion followed by registration. China distinguishes registration involving assessment of safety, health function, and quality controllability from catalog-based filing supported by technical documentation. Chinese health foods and European food supplements are not identical legal categories. The examples demonstrate the importance of total exposure, preparation specific toxicity, and continued reassessment after market entry. An administrative status or regulatory dose ceiling cannot establish universal safety or therapeutic efficacy. Conclusion: Good practice combines transparent classification, proportionate evidence requirements, prominent warnings, controlled product changes, and post-market surveillance. Chinese functional assessment adds a distinct comparator but does not establish superiority in health outcomes. The review supports cooperation between legal, toxicological, nutritional, and clinical expertise, while identifying limits arising from documentary access and the absence of comparative outcome data.

title: The specifics of using digital tools in political and economic communication and ways to determine their economic effectiveness
journal: JOURNAL OF MONETARY ECONOMICS AND MANAGEMENT
abstract: The field of digital communication in politics is of interest for research, since the development of any social system is closely linked to competent political decision-making. The need for sustainable and high-quality information transfer must have an appropriate level of attention to its tools in order to ensure the effectiveness of all necessary processes. Digital means of communication are able to reach their potential precisely in this environment, since their prerogative is effective communication between subjects. It is necessary to understand how important it is for citizens to be able to quickly and easily communicate their public opinion, file a complaint or a proposal, and solve their widespread problems without making lengthy entries to the necessary government structure. And civil servants will find out about them faster and respond promptly. In recent years, there has been relatively intensive scientific work in the field of thesis defense on the topic of political and network communications. However, it should be recognized that most of them explore the Internet either from the point of view of sociology, psychology, journalism, or are related to other areas of political communication theory. The topic under study is of great interest both abroad and in Russia, both from a practical and theoretical point of view. It should be noted that, despite the tradition of serious study of political and economic communication in Russia and abroad, there is a need for new research in the field of network technologies of political communication and their impact social transformations caused by both new research tasks and the extreme dynamism of the development of network communications.

title: The Landscape Of Global Technological Competition: A Us–China Bilateral Analysis
journal: The Journal of Interdisciplinary Human Studies
abstract: This paper analyses the dynamic landscape of global technological competition, focusing on the strategic and bilateral friction between the United States and China. It examines critical socio-technical domains, including artificial intelligence, semiconductor manufacturing, quantum computing, 5G/6G telecommunications and green technologies. The study highlights how the contemporary technology sector is governed by market mechanisms such as the “winner-takes-all” paradigm, the global talent war and intensive patent warfare. Furthermore, the paper evaluates the shifting regulatory frameworks of the US–China rivalry, characterised by a transition from total embargoes to case-by-case reviews in the semiconductor industry, coupled with strategic countermeasures involving critical raw materials. Finally, it outlines the “dual-track strategy” employed by Washington and Beijing, which balances offensive geopolitical containment in strategic sectors with pragmatic, managed trade reciprocity and risk- mitigation dialogues in non-strategic domains in order to maintain macroeconomic stability.

title: SEO as a tool for managing the company's digital presence
journal: JOURNAL OF MONETARY ECONOMICS AND MANAGEMENT
abstract: This article explores the role of search engine optimization (SEO) as a strategic management tool for a company's digital presence. Using a comparative analysis of industry data, it examines the dynamics of the global SEO software market and the bipolar structure of the Russian search market: Yandex relies on behavioral factors, while Google prioritizes content quality and reputation. This divergence requires Russian companies to pursue two coordinated, yet distinct, optimization strategies. The ROI of digital channels is analyzed: SEO delivers the highest long-term returns, although the payback period ranges from nine to sixteen months. The impact of AI Overviews blocks is also examined: their proliferation has led to a significant drop in organic click-through rates and has brought GEO (Generative Response Evaluation) to the forefront: a strategy aimed at reaching cited sources of generative responses. The results are intended for digital marketing and corporate management professionals.

title: Drying behavior, thermodynamic properties, and functional stability of taioba starch enriched with leaf bioactive extracts
journal: Journal of Food Measurement and Characterization
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the drying kinetics, thermodynamic properties, physicochemical characteristics, bioactive compounds, and antioxidant activity of native and enriched taioba starches obtained from Xanthosoma sagittifolium . Native starch (CS) and starches enriched with in natura extract (ES-I), decoction extract (ES-D), and steam-treated extract (ES-V) were dried at 30, 40, and 50 °C. Drying behavior was modeled using mathematical equations, with the Midilli model providing the best fit to the experimental data. Increasing drying temperature significantly reduced drying time and enhanced effective moisture diffusivity, with values ranging from 1.84 × 10⁻¹⁰ to 8.55 × 10⁻¹⁰ m²/s. Enriched starches showed lower diffusivity values than native starch, indicating interactions between starch and bioactive compounds that reduced water mobility during drying. Arrhenius analysis demonstrated that the extracts modified activation energy and thermal sensitivity of the starch matrices. Thermodynamic properties revealed an endothermic and non-spontaneous drying process, characterized by positive Gibbs free energy and negative entropy values. Physicochemical analyses showed low moisture content and water activity, contributing to improved storage stability. Taioba leaves exhibited high concentrations of phenolic compounds, carotenoids, chlorophylls, flavonoids, anthocyanins, and ascorbic acid, resulting in elevated antioxidant activity. Enrichment significantly increased the bioactive content and antioxidant capacity of starches, especially in ES-I treatments. The results demonstrate that taioba leaf extracts are promising natural sources of bioactive compounds and that enriched taioba starches present potential for application as functional ingredients in food systems.

title: Combating Cyberbullying and Child Online Exploitation in Nigeria: Legal Strategies and Enforcement Realities
journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technologies and internet access has transformed communication, education, and social interaction globally. This digital revolution, however, has also exposed children to increasing risks of cyberbullying, online grooming, sextortion, child sexual abuse materials (CSAM), and other forms of technology-facilitated exploitation. In Nigeria, the growing number of young internet users, coupled with limited digital literacy and inadequate online safeguards, has heightened children's vulnerability to cyber-related harms. This paper examines the legal and institutional strategies adopted to combat cyberbullying and child online exploitation in Nigeria, with particular emphasis on enforcement realities. Using a doctrinal and comparative legal research methodology, the study analyzes relevant legal frameworks, including the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act 2015, the Child Rights Act 2003, constitutional provisions, and data protection regulations. It further evaluates the roles of key enforcement institutions such as the Nigeria Police Force, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, the Nigerian Communications Commission, and other agencies. The paper identifies significant enforcement challenges, including inadequate technical capacity, weak inter-agency coordination, low reporting rates, societal stigmatization of victims, judicial limitations, and insufficient international cooperation. Drawing lessons from legal and institutional approaches adopted in the United Kingdom, the United States, and South Africa, the study highlights best practices that may strengthen Nigeria's response to online child abuse. The paper concludes by recommending comprehensive legal reforms, with specialized enforcement mechanisms, to ensure effective protection of fundamental rights of children in the digital environment and in cyberspace.
